take_homes: Seats and licences measure access, not use. I should ask for the usage and trust figure, not the roll-out figure.
Before any rollout, ask what would have to be true for the person to drop what they use today (my controller's spreadsheet).
An empty owner field is the real risk in a plan. Name who answers for the thing first.

monday.move: Ask my controller how she writes the month-end variance commentary today, and who would answer for an agent doing it. Test one assumption: that her current way is slow enough to switch from.
monday.when: Monday, a 15-minute conversation, after month-end close
monday.stop_condition: If she says the current way is fine and can't say what would have to be better, I drop it. I also stop if it would mean putting finance data into a tool IT hasn't approved.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: I came in thinking AI is a licence you buy. The line that access and absorption get reported as one number made me see that the licence is the easy bit. The story of the proposal that got no decision backed it up. Nothing here showed what absorbing it costs, so I'm not fully convinced it's a capability the organisation builds.

one_line: Honest and short on hype, and it says buying the tool is the easy part. But there's not a single cost or payback figure in it.
